Record Class PythonModuleMapping

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.micronaut.python.imports.PythonModuleMapping
Record Components:
module - The Python module name, such as pyronaut.http
documentation - The module documentation, shown by editors, or null
sources - The sources of the exported names, in precedence order
prefer - The explicit winners of clashes: Python name to the binary name of the winning type (the declaring type for a static method or an enum constant)
preferredPackages - The packages whose names win the clashes they take part in, in precedence order, once an explicit preference and PythonModuleMapping.ClashPolicy.PREFER_ANNOTATIONS have not decided
clashPolicy - How the clashes that neither prefer nor preferredPackages decide are decided
exclude - The Python names left out of the module
replaces - Whether this contribution replaces the contributions of lower precedence to the same module instead of merging with them
requiredArtifact - The coordinates of the artifact providing the first source, named in the error reported when the module is imported without it, or null
public record PythonModuleMapping(String module, @Nullable String documentation, List<PythonModuleMapping.Source> sources, Map<String,String> prefer, List<String> preferredPackages, PythonModuleMapping.ClashPolicy clashPolicy, Set<String> exclude, boolean replaces, @Nullable String requiredArtifact) extends Record
The definition of a curated Python module: the Java sources whose names it exports, in precedence order, and how the names two sources both export are decided.

A clash, a name exported by more than one source for different targets, is decided by the first rule that applies: an explicit preferred target for the name; with PythonModuleMapping.ClashPolicy.PREFER_ANNOTATIONS, the only annotation among the candidates; a preferred package one of the candidates belongs to; then the clash policy: an error with PythonModuleMapping.ClashPolicy.FAIL, else the first source.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Graeme Rocher
